findings.message: The diff changes plugin code and hooks under plugins/specclaw (new hook, new verify subcommand, mod changes, config template) but bumps no version. Bump every plugins/*/.claude-plugin/plugin.json, every plugins/*/.codex-plugin/plugin.json and every plugins[] entry in .claude-plugin/marketplace.json to the same new version.
findings.scenario: Plugin code changes ship, but all version fields stay at the old value, so installed copies see no update and the hook and `specclaw-verify size` never reach existing users.

findings.message: `cmd_size` reports 'not counted' and returns 0 when no base is found. It also treats a failing `git diff` as 0 lines, because the pipeline hides the git exit status. 'Could not ask' therefore reads as 'under the cap'. Exit nonzero or print a distinct unknown state (verify then records it as not run), and check git's exit status before summing.
findings.scenario: A CI checkout is shallow, or has no origin/main and no local main. `specclaw-verify size` prints 'no base branch to compare with, not counted' and exits 0, so a 5000-line change passes the size cap.

findings.message: The base-branch resolution is written twice and the copies disagree. branch.ts matches `base_branch:` anywhere in config.yaml, while lib/base-ref.sh reads it only under the `git:` block. branch.ts also resolves origin/HEAD with `rev-parse --abbrev-ref` instead of symbolic-ref. The branch guard and the done guard / size cap can therefore pick different base branches. Scope the TS regex to the `git:` block, or share one resolver.
findings.scenario: config.yaml has `git:\n  base_branch: main` and another key elsewhere, such as a `fleet:` block with `base_branch: develop`. The TS regex takes the first match in the file, which may be `develop`. The branch guard then holds edits on `develop` and allows them on `main`, while done-guard and size diff against `main`.

findings.message: `onBaseBranch` swallows every failure with `catch { return undefined }`, and a non-zero git exit also returns '' with no toast. The branch guard silently turns off. R2 allows failing open but requires the error to be surfaced with a toast. Notify when the read or git call throws, as opposed to the legitimate 'detached HEAD / not in git' case.
findings.scenario: `$.fs.read` of config.yaml throws, or `git` times out after 3000 ms. `onBaseBranch` returns undefined and the Write to main runs with no toast, so the operator never learns the guard did not run.

findings.message: The verify verdict is parsed with line-based `grep -oE '"verify"...\{[^}]*\}'` on state.json. This only works when the verify object sits on one line and has no nested braces. A pretty-printed or multi-line state.json yields an empty `verify`, which reports a false 'no verify verdict' and traps the Stop. The tests only plant single-line hand-written JSON (B2), not output from `specclaw-set-phase`. Read the field with a real JSON parser, and drive the tests through the real writer.
findings.scenario: `specclaw-set-phase` (or any tool) writes state.json as multi-line JSON with `"verify": {` on one line and `"verdict": "PASS"` on the next. `grep -o` finds no match, so the guard exits 2 with 'no verify verdict' for a change that passed.
